analysis:
Both units are head-side text of docs/developer/test.md (lines 1311-2219). They contain documentation only, with no executable, auth, crypto, or config changes. The security-relevant statements are guidance for test hygiene and scope limits.

Relevant statements:
- Lines 1385-1419 describe the App Attest validation and provider session reliability tests. They keep the boundaries between worker transport, lifecycle and qualification (TB-011, T-053, T-057). They state that signing is not Apple acceptance and that transport fixtures are not serving qualification. Opt-in native failures must not be turned into skips. This is consistent with the threat model (T-052, T-056).
- Lines 1317-1343 cover the cache scope fixture. It states it does not qualify multi-host routing, signed key durability or hosted account trust. This is consistent with the T-041 posture of account-scoped cacheSalt.
- Lines 1837-1846 and 1692-1715 tell the reader to use disposable databases only, never production DATABASE_URL. They describe per-process isolated databases.
- Lines 1757-1760 instruct clearing inherited service, database, auth and telemetry variables. They also state the transport rejects proxies and redirects.
- Lines 2184-2200 describe synthetic fixtures with no production credentials.

No new attack surface, no invalidated assumptions, and no claim of production qualification. The threat model needs no update from this PR. Cross-file checks for integration: the referenced test files and paths (e.g. AppAttestShadowReplyTests, WorkerTransportTests) are not shown in this batch, so it is unverified that they exist and match the descriptions. This is a documentation-accuracy coverage limit, not a security finding.
